characters.name: Aura Beinhaven
characters.notes:
Aura is a squad leader in Fourth Wing until Xaden Riorson moves her to Second Wing in order to place Violet Sorrengail under his command. Aura begins her duties as senior wingleader of the quadrant as a third-year cadet.[4] She accuses Dain of lying when he tells the cadets that their leadership has been hiding the venin issue from them. She threatens Dain with a dagger. Garrick steps in to stop her, aided by Heaton, Emery, and Cianna. Aura is still in a fighting stance after Violet's dragon Tairn shares memories of a fight with venin with the whole formation, implying that she remains loyal to Navarre and stays at Basgiath. After Xaden Riorsen becomes a professor of Basgiath temporarily, Aura joins the ranks of Colonel Aetos' minions that spy on both Xaden and Violet in an attempt to catch the two in any misdeeds that could allow Colonel Aetos to dismiss Xaden from Basgiath. Aura prowls the dormitories where Violet's rooms are located in an attempt to give Aetos a reason to punish Violet for a violation of the codex. During the mission to retrieve the Amelian Citrine for the king of Deverelli, Aura disobeys Mira's order to not wield (so as not to draw the attention of any Venin that might be nearby). Aura is left with Violet when the leadership of the mission walk off to discuss where to look for the Citrine, when Aura lets her fear overcome her. A glass bottle rolls towards the pair which causes Aura to remove her gloves to reveal a flint sparking device held between her thumb and forefinger. Just then a door across the street swung open with an ear screeching creak, and a figure stepped out of the shadows, startling both cadets. In that moment Violet attempts to stop Aura from channeling, and Aura inadvertently engulfs Captain Grady in a wave of fire, thinking he was a Venin.

A horrified Aura watches as the Captain is covered in foot high flames, as Violet takes command in an attempt to put out the fire. The flames jump to the building near them, and Captain Grady goes quiet in death.

While the wind wielder in their party attempts to put out the fire, the entire town goes up in flames like a tinder-box. Aura freezes in shock and must be dragged up and out by Mira Sorrengail, as they attempt to find a way out of the fire. As they run for the town square (the only area open enough for the riders dragons can land) Aura says "This is my fault. Grady is... gone, they'll know we're here, there's no hiding a fire like this".

After Mira Sorrengail leaps upon her dragon Teine, Aura is told she is next as her dragon approaches. Aura sprints forward into the open in preparation to mount her dragon when a Wyvern swoops in, picks her up with a claw through the middle of her spine and blood gushes from the wound. Aura's scream is silenced as the Wyvern drags her lifeless body into the sky, and there is a corresponding dragon bellow as Dagoth mourns for his rider. There is absolutely no doubt that Aura is dead.

characters.name: Amber Mavis
characters.notes:
Put to death on page 246 of Fourth Wing 
Amber Mavis was the wingleader from Third Wing and close friend of Dain Aetos.When Violet is attacked in her room, Amber is revealed to be the one who let the attackers in. Xaden Riorson accused her of violating Article Three, Section Two of the Dragon Rider's Codex, a capital offense, during formation. The wingleaders formed a quorum and found Amber guilty by unanimous agreement after Violet's dragon, Tairneanach, shared her memory of the attack with everyone present. After initially having denied involvement, Amber declares that it is not a crime to rid the quadrant of the weakest rider, explaining that she did it to protect the integrity of the wings. Tairneanach carries out the sentence of execution by dragon fire.

characters.name: Alic Tauri Baran
characters.notes: Prince Alic Tauri Baran was the second son of King Tauri and the twin brother of Halden Tauri, the Crown Prince of Navarre.[1] A cadet in the Riders Quadrant, he bullied the marked ones at Basgiath War College and was killed by Xaden Riorson during their Threshing on October 1, 631 AU, after holding Garrick Tavis at knifepoint. notices.title: Public Notice 634.23
notices.summary: Conscription rates are doubled in every province until further notice.
notices.text: Conscription rates are hereby doubled for each province until further notice.

notices.title: Public Notice 628.86
notices.summary: After the Treaty of Aretia, Tyrrendor's seat in the King's Senarium passes from House Riorson to House Lewellen.
notices.text: As a result of the Treaty of Aretia, the power to represent the province of Tyrrendor in the King’s Senarium has hereby been transferred from the House of Riorson to the House of Lewellen.

notices.title: Public Notice 628.85
notices.summary: Records that Aretia was burned by dragons under the treaty that ended the separatist movement. Those who fled, survived, the rest remain entombed in the ruins.
notices.text: In this, the 628th year of our Unification, it is hereby recorded that Aretia has been burned by dragon in accordance with the Treaty ending the separatist movement. Those who fled, survived, and those who did not remain entombed in her ruins.

notices.title: Public Notice 442.184
notices.summary: Raiders from the Emerald Sea sacked the Tyrrish village of Kyllendelle. Seaside residents of Tyrrendor and Luceras are asked to stay vigilant and light warning beacons to call the nearest riot.
notices.text: The Tyrrish village of Kyllendelle has been sacked by raiders from the Emerald Sea. We ask those living by the seaside in Tyrrendor and Luceras to remain vigilant in service to their fellow Navarrians and light the warning beacons to alert the nearest riot if requesting aid.

notices.title: Public Notice 433.231
notices.summary: Navarrian forces repelled an attempted breach by Poromish troops near the outpost of Athebyne. The attack is called unprovoked, and the commitment to the peace process is restated.
notices.text: Our forces have successfully routed an attempted breach of our border by Poromish forces near the outpost of Athebyne. While this attack was unprovoked, we remain committed to the peace process.

notices.title: Public Notice 210.183
notices.summary: Provincial notices are ended. Regional notices written by local scribes replace them, each needing approval from the Curator of the Scribe Quadrant at Basgiath before posting.
notices.text: The system of provincial notices is hereby ended in order to simplify the flow of accurate information to all Navarrians, and will be replaced with regional notices provided by local scribes, all of which must be approved by the Curator of the Scribe Quadrant of Basgiath War College before posting.

notices.title: Public Notice 209.11
notices.summary: Public notices now override provincial ones, posted for up to sixty days in any village with more than five hundred people.
notices.text: In the interest of quelling rumor and providing accurate information on behalf of the crown, all public notices hereby transcend their provincial counterparts, and will be posted for a maximum of sixty days in any village with a population greater than five hundred.

notices.title: Public Notice 208.271
notices.summary: Queen Alondra splits Tyrrendor into three duchies (Lewellen, Tirvainne and Aretia). The Duchess of Aretia keeps the Tyrrish seat on the Senarium.
notices.text: Queen Alondra has ordered the provinces of Tyrrendor to be split into three duchies to better serve her citizens. While the Dukes of Lewellen and Tirvainne will oversee their territories for the betterment of all—as per the new maps provided by the crown—the Duchess of Aretia will retain the Tyrrish seat on the Senarium to represent the province.

notices.title: Public Notice 207.6
notices.summary: Because of increased danger, travel beyond Navarre may only be authorized by the sovereign.
notices.text: Due to increased danger to our citizens, travel beyond Navarre may only be authorized by the sovereign.

notices.title: Public Notice 207.1
notices.summary: Every duchy signs a Provincial Commitment placing the provincial armies under Queen Alondra's standard against Poromish aggression until the war is declared over.
notices.text: A Provincial Commitment has been signed by every duchy in Navarre, consolidating the provinces' armies under Queen Alondra's standard to better defend our kingdom against Poromish aggression until such time as the war is declared over.

notices.title: Public Notice 200.417
notices.summary: Guardians may no longer dedicate children to a favored deity. Serving the gods for life must be chosen freely after the age of majority.
notices.text: Guardians are no longer permitted to dedicate children in service to their favored deity. The decision to serve the gods for life must be made after the age of majority and of one’s free will.

notices.title: Public Notice 2.21
notices.summary: The Migration of the First Year is declared complete. Borders are secured against increasingly militant neighbors, and travel beyond Navarre may be authorized by a duchy's ruling house.
notices.text: The triumphant success of The Migration of The First Year is now considered complete. To keep the promise of peace we fought for, our forces have taken the unfortunate, but necessary precaution of securing our borders against our increasingly militant neighbors. Travel beyond Navarre may be authorized by a duchy's ruling house.

notices.title: Public Notice 1.323
notices.summary: Krovlan forces attacked Elsum, causing four casualties in the mountains near the village of Resson. The area is secured and the attack is called an outlier; the commitment to peace stands.
notices.text: The province of Elsum has suffered an unprovoked attack by Krovlan forces, resulting in four casualties in the mountains near the village of Resson. The area has been secured. Our commitment to peace has not wavered and we consider this heinous act to be an outlier.

notices.title: Public Notice 1.249
notices.summary: The Council of Calldyr agrees that Navarre is ruled as a secular kingdom, but its marriage law follows the terms each god sets in their temples.
notices.text: The Council of Calldyr has agreed that while rule of Navarre is secular, the law of the kingdom will follow the unique terms each god has set in their temples regarding marriage.

notices.title: Public Notice 1.3
notices.summary: As promised in the Unification Scrolls, the borders stay open for twelve months to anyone who wants to live under Navarre's wards and laws.
notices.text: As promised in the Unification Scrolls that define our laws, for the next twelve months, the borders of the Kingdom of Navarre will remain open to all who wish to live under the protection of our wards and laws. We welcome all who wish to be Navarrians.

notices.title: Public Notice 1.2
notices.summary: The scribes of Basgiath War College take over announcing and recording public notices, posted beside provincial ones for at least thirty days in villages with more than fifty people.
notices.text: In the interest of the security of Navarre and in the spirit of transparency within our unified realm, the scribes of Basgiath War College have assumed the honorable responsibility of announcing and recording all pertinent information via public notices. These notices shall be posted alongside their provincial counterparts for a minimum of thirty days in any village with a population greater than fifty.

notices.title: Public Notice 1.1
notices.summary: Calldyr, Elsum, Luceras, Morraine and Tyrrendor accept the Unification Scrolls and swear fealty to King Reginald Navarrius. The kingdom is named Navarre and the calendar restarts at year 1.
notices.text: It is hereby recorded that the territories of Calldyr, Elsum, Luceras, Morraine, and Tyrrendor have agreed to terms defined in the Unification Scrolls and sworn fealty to our magnanimous King Reginald Navarrius. All people dwelling within the safe haven of our borders shall be considered citizens of the kingdom now known as Navarre. In celebration of this momentous occasion and our new, peaceful era, our calendars shall reflect this year as our first after unification.

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 1
notices.text:
A dragon without its rider is a tragedy. A rider without their dragon is dead.
— Article One, Section One, The Dragon Rider's Codex

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 2
notices.text:
There's a misconception that it's kill or be killed in the Riders Quadrant. Riders, as a whole, aren't out to assassinate other cadets... unless there's a shortage of dragons that year or a cadet is a liability to their wing. Then things may get... interesting.
— Major Affendra's Guide to the Riders Quadrant, Unauthorized Edition

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 3
notices.text:
Blue dragons descend from the extraordinary Gormfaileas line. Known for their formidable size, they are the most ruthless, especially in the case of the rare blue dagger tail, whose knife-like spikes at the tip of their tail can disembowel an enemy with one flick.
— Colonel Kaori's Field Guide to Dragonkind

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 4
notices.text:
The sparring ring is where riders are made or broken. After all, no respectable dragon would choose a rider who cannot defend themselves, and no respectable cadet would allow such a threat to the wing to continue training.
— Major Afendra's Guide to the Riders Quadrant, Unauthorized Edition

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 5
notices.text:
Knowing I am in direct disagreement with General Melgren's orders, I am officially objecting to the plan set forth in today's briefing. It is not this general's opinion that the children of the rebellion's leaders should be forced to witness their parents' executions. No child should watch their parent put to death.
— The Tyrrish Rebellion, an Official Brief for King Tauri by General Lilith Sorrengail

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 6
notices.text:
It is my opinion that of all the signet powers riders provide, mending is the most precious, but we cannot allow ourselves to become complacent in the company of such a signet. For menders are rare, and the wounded are not.
— Major Frederick's Modern Guide for Healers

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 7
notices.text:
In the best interest of preserving peace within Navarre, no more than three cadets carrying rebellion relics may be assigned to any squad of any quadrant.
— Addendum 5.2, Basgiath War College Code of Conduct

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 8
notices.text:
In addition to last year's changes, Marked Ones assembling in groups of three or more will now be considered an act of seditious conspiracy and is hereby a capital offense.
— Addendum 5.3, Basgiath War College Code of Conduct

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 9
notices.text:
There is an art to poison not often discussed, and that is timing. Only a master can properly dose and administer for effective onset. One must take into account the mass of the individual as well as the method of delivery.
— Effective Uses of Wild and Cultivated Herbs by Captain Lawrence Medina

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 10
notices.text:
I will not die today.
— Violet Sorrengail's personal addendum to the Book of Brennan

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 11
notices.text:
Don't underestimate the challenge of the gauntlet, Mira. It's designed to test your balance, strength, and agility. The times don't matter for shit, only that you make it to the top. Reach for the ropes when you have to. Coming in last is better than coming in dead.
— Page 46, the Book of Brennan

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 12
notices.text:
It is a grave offense against Malek to keep the belongings of a dead loved one. They belong to the beyond with the god of death and the departed. In the absence of a proper temple, any fire will do. He who does not burn for Malek will be burned by Malek.
— Major Rorilee's Guide to Appeasing the Gods, Second Edition

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 13
notices.text:
Presentation Day is unlike any other. The air is ripe with possibilities and possibly the stench of sulfur from a dragon who's been offended. Never look a red in the eye, never back down from a green. If you show trepidation to a brown... well, just don't.
— Colonel Kaori's Field Guide to Dragonkind

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 14
notices.text:
There is nothing quite as humbling or as awe-inspiring as witnessing Threshing. For those who live through it, anyway.
— Colonel Kaori's Field Guide to Dragonkind

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 15
notices.text:
In the six centuries of recorded history of dragon and rider, there have been hundreds of known cases where a dragon simply cannot emotionally recover from the loss of their bonded rider. This happens when the bond is particularly strong, and in three documented cases, it has even caused the untimely death of the dragon.
— Navarre: An Unedited History by Colonel Lewis Markham

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 16
notices.text:
Just because you survive Threshing doesn't mean you'll survive the ride to the flight field. Being chosen isn't the only test, and if you can't hold your seat, then you'll fly straight into the ground.
— Page 50, the Book of Brennan

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 17
notices.text:
Though this officer considers himself to be an expert on all matters dragonkind, there is a great deal we don't know about the way dragons govern themselves. There is a clear hierarchy among the most powerful and deference is paid to elders, but I have not been able to discern how it is they make laws for themselves or at what point a dragon decided to bond only one rider rather than go for the better odds with two.
— Colonel Kaori's Field Guide to Dragonkind

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 18
notices.text:
It is therefore only natural that the more powerful the dragon, the more powerful the signet its rider manifests. One should be wary of a strong rider who bonds a smaller dragon, but even warier of the unbonded cadet who will stop at nothing to seize a chance to bond.
— Major Afendra's Guide to the Riders Quadrant, Unauthorized Edition

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 19
notices.text:
There is nothing more sacred than the archives. Even temples can be rebuilt, but books cannot be rewritten.
— Colonel Daxton's Guide to Excelling in the Scribe Quadrant

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 20
notices.text:
In response to the Great War, dragons claimed the western lands and the gryphons the central ones, abandoning the Barrens and the memory of General Daramor, who nearly destroyed the continent with his army. Our allies sailed home and we began a period of peace and prosperity as the provinces of Navarre united for the first time behind the safety of our wards under the protection of the first bonded riders.
— Navarre: An Unedited History by Colonel Lewis Markham

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 21
notices.text:
Accusing a wing leader of wrongdoing is the most dangerous of all accusations. If you're right, then we failed as a quadrant to select the best wing leaders. If you're wrong, you're dead.
— My Time as a Cadet, a memoir by General Augustine Melgren

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 22
notices.text:
Don't freak out if you can't immediately channel your dragon's powers, Mira. Yeah, I know you have to be the best at everything, but this isn't something you can control. They'll channel when they feel you're ready, and once they do, you'd better be ready to manifest a signet. Until then, you're not ready, don't push it.
— Page 61, the Book of Brennan

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 23
notices.text:
The first rush of power is unmistakable. The first time it forms to you, surrounds you with a seemingly endless supply of energy. You'll be addicted to the high, to the possibilities of all you can do with it, to the control you hold in the palm of your hand. But here's the thing, that power can quickly turn and control you.
— Page 64, the Book of Brennan

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 24
notices.text:
The most worrisome sight for any instructor is most definitely when powers backfire. We lost nine cadets in my first year to signets that could not be controlled from their first manifestation. Pity.
— Major Affendra's Guide to the Riders Quadrant, Unauthorized Edition

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 25
notices.text:
I know you don't want to hear this, but sometimes you have to know when to take the death blow, Mira. That's why you have to be sure that Violet enters the Scribe Quadrant [? you said "supply quadrant"]. She'll never be able to take a life.
— Page 70, the Book of Brennan

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 26
notices.text:
There is no stronger bond than that between two mated dragons. It goes beyond the depth of human love or adoration to a primal, undeniable requirement for proximity. One cannot survive without the other.
— Colonel Kaori's Field Guide to Dragonkind

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 27
notices.text:
For valor above and beyond the call of duty in the Battle of Strathmore, where her bravery resulted not only in the destruction of a battery behind enemy lines, but also saved the lives of an entire company of infantry, I recommend Mira Sorrengail receive the Star of Navarre. But if the criterion is not met, which I assure you it has been, downgrading to the Order of the Talon would be a shame, but sufficient.
— Recommendation for Award from Major Potsdam to General Sorrengail

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 28
notices.text:
Winning the war games isn't about strength, it's about cunning. To know how to strike, you have to understand where your enemies, your friends, are most vulnerable. No one stays friends forever, Mira. Eventually, those closest to us become our enemies in some way, even if it's through well-intentioned love or apathy, or if we live long enough to become their villains.
— Page 80, the Book of Brennan

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 29
notices.text:
The death of a cadet is an inevitable yet acceptable tragedy. This process thins the herd, leaving only the strongest riders. As long as the cause of death does not break the codex, any rider involved in extinguishing another's life shall not be punished.
— Major Affendra's Guide to the Riders Quadrant, Unauthorized Edition

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 30
notices.text:
Though not forbidden, cadets are strongly encouraged not to develop strong romantic attachments while studying in the quadrant for the efficiency of the unit.
— Article 5, Section 7, the Dragon Rider's Codex

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 31
notices.text:
July 1st, the anniversary of the Battle of Aretia, is hereby proclaimed Reunification Day and will be celebrated throughout Navarre on this date every year to honor the lives lost during the war to save our kingdom from separatists and those saved by the Treaty of Aretia.
— Royal Proclamation of King Tauri the Wise

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 32
notices.text:
As for the 107 innocents, the children of the executed officers, they now carry what shall be known as the Rebellion Relic, transferred by the dragon who carried out the justice, the king's justice, and to show the mercy of our great king. They will all be conscripted to the prestigious Riders Quadrant at Basgiath, so they may prove their loyalty to our kingdom with their service or with their death.
— Addendum 4.2, the Treaty of Aretia

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 33
notices.text:
The inability to control a powerful signet is just as dangerous to a rider and everyone in their vicinity as never manifesting one.
— Major Affendra's Guide to the Riders Quadrant, Unauthorized Edition

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 34
notices.text:
The first known gryphon attack occurred in 1 AU, after unification, near what is now the trading post of Resson. At the edge of the dragon-protected border, the post has always been vulnerable to attack, and over the course of the past six centuries has changed hands no less than eleven times in what has become a never-ending war to secure our borders from our power-hungry enemies.
— Navarre: An Unedited History by Colonel Lewis Markham

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 35
notices.text:
In his last days of interrogation, Fen Riorson lost touch with reality, railing against the kingdom of Navarre. He accused King Tauri and all who came before him of a conspiracy so vast, so unspeakable, that it does not bear repeating by this historian. The execution was swift and merciful for a madman who caused untold lives.
— Navarre: An Unedited History by Colonel Lewis Markham

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 36
notices.text:
For there, in the land beyond the shadows, were monsters that dwelled in the night and dined on the souls of children who wandered too close to the woods. The wyvern's cry, [?]. But it was the third brother who commanded the sky to surrender its greatest power, who finally vanquished the jealous sibling at a great and terrible price.
— The Origin, Fables of the [? Barren / Baron]

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 37
notices.text:
In the event that you come across a poison you do not recognize, it is best to treat it with any and every antidote. Either way, the patient will die, but at least this way you would have learned something.
— Major Frederick's Modern Guide for Healers

notices.title: Fourth Wing — Chapter 38
notices.text:
You're all cowards.
— The last words of Fen Riorson, redacted
